name: Maas
title: Levite and Temple Musician
summary: Maas (also spelled Maaseiah) is a name that appears several times in the Old Testament, particularly in connection with the return from exile in Babylon. He was among the Levites and priests who served in the temple after its rebuilding and actively participated in the reforms under Ezra and Nehemiah. The name means 'the Lord's work' and is borne by several individuals involved in worship, praise, and spiritual renewal in restored Israel.

keyEvents.title: Among Those Who Had Taken Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: Maas was among the priests who had taken foreign wives and committed to sending them away during Ezra's reform.

keyEvents.title: Participation in the Reading of the Law
keyEvents.description: Maas stood beside Ezra when the law was read aloud to the people at the Water Gate, helping them understand God's word.

keyEvents.title: Contribution to the Dedication of Jerusalem's Wall
keyEvents.description: Maas took part in the great celebration and dedication of Jerusalem's rebuilt wall under Nehemiah's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the Levites who led worship
keyEvents.description: Maas is mentioned among the Levites who led the people in worship and praise after returning from exile.

keyEvents.title: The Sealing of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Maas was among those who put their seal on the covenant to follow God's law during the renewal of the covenant in Nehemiah's time.
